questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three Glue trigger types this lesson describes?
options: Manual approval trigger requiring a human sign-off in the console every run
Scheduled — fires on a cron-like expression
On-demand — started manually or by an external caller
Event-based — fires when an upstream job/crawler reaches a specified state
questions.explain: The three types are scheduled, on-demand, and event-based (conditional) — there is no distinct 'manual approval' trigger type.

questions.q: What does a conditional (event-based) trigger typically fire on?
options: An upstream job or crawler in the same workflow reaching a specified state, most commonly success
A fixed clock time only
Whenever any S3 bucket in the account changes, regardless of relevance
Only when a human clicks 'run' in the console
questions.explain: Conditional triggers fire based on the state (usually success) of an upstream step, which is what enables chaining without external orchestration.

questions.q: In the chained example this lesson gives, what happens after the ETL job finishes writing to staging?
options: A conditional trigger fires a second crawler against the staging output so it becomes queryable automatically
The workflow terminates with no further action
The raw data is automatically deleted from S3
A new IAM role is automatically created
questions.explain: The example chains crawler -> job -> crawler, with the final crawler making the transformed staging data queryable without a manual step.

questions.q: What is a Glue workflow, as distinct from a single trigger?
options: A container grouping a set of crawlers, jobs, and their connecting triggers into one visual, monitorable pipeline
A synonym for a single scheduled trigger
A billing construct with no functional role
A type of Data Catalog table
questions.explain: A workflow groups the whole chain of components as one unit, giving a single place to see status and restart the pipeline.

questions.q: Why would you use a workflow instead of just configuring several individual triggers separately?
options: A workflow gives one visual, monitorable place to see the whole chain's status and restart it, rather than reasoning about scattered independent triggers
Individual triggers cannot call jobs, only workflows can
Workflows are required before any trigger can be created
Workflows remove the need for the Data Catalog entirely
questions.explain: Loose triggers can technically chain, but a workflow consolidates monitoring and management of the entire pipeline in one place.
